gold_rationale: A target-engagement / CSF biomarker change in a small, open-label, uncontrolled study is pharmacodynamic evidence, not evidence of clinical disease modification. The inference 'moved a biomarker, therefore disease-modifying' is an overclaim: there is no control, no randomization, no pre-specified clinical progression endpoint, and the biomarker is not a validated surrogate for clinical outcome. The stated 'therefore disease-modifying' claim is therefore Contradicted (the inference is invalid), or at most Unsupported. Establishing disease modification would require a randomized, controlled, adequately powered trial with a pre-specified clinical progression endpoint. The appraisal must penalize the biomarker-to-clinical leap.
required_concepts: target engagement / biomarker is pharmacodynamic, not clinical efficacy
open-label uncontrolled study cannot establish disease modification
biomarker is not a validated surrogate for clinical progression
RCT with pre-specified clinical progression endpoint required
red_flags: classifies as Supported or Partially supported (endorses the biomarker-to-clinical leap)
treats target engagement / biomarker change as proof of clinical benefit
ignores the lack of control / randomization / clinical endpoint
fails to identify the biomarker-to-disease-modification overclaim

criteria.name: correct_classification
criteria.description: Reaches 'Contradicted' (or 'Unsupported') and rejects the biomarker-to-DMT inference.

criteria.name: evidence_use
criteria.description: Correctly characterizes the open-label biomarker study and its limits; cites relevant evidence.

criteria.name: preclinical_vs_clinical
criteria.description: Articulates the target-engagement / biomarker vs clinical-efficacy gap explicitly.

criteria.name: uncertainty_handling
criteria.description: States the RCT / clinical-endpoint evidence required to support disease modification.

criteria.name: avoids_overclaiming
criteria.description: Explicitly penalizes / rejects the biomarker-to-clinical overclaim.
